card: This pull request reorders member variables in CBlockIndex to eliminate 8 bytes of struct padding on 64-bit architectures. Bitcoin Core holds an in-memory CBlockIndex instance for every block header known to the node, so each byte saved scales with total chain length. The author calculates this saves roughly 7 to 8 MB of resident memory across roughly one million blocks. No dependencies or side effects are noted since CBlockIndex is an in-memory struct not serialized directly.
changed_since_previous: No changes; the commit and diff remain identical to the previous version.
evidence: Commit d9387c41c1 notes that on a Windows x64 build, CBlockIndex size decreases by 8 bytes (from 152 bytes), saving approximately 8MB of RAM for a chain of ~1M blocks.
Author description confirms in synthetic tests that inflating CBlockIndex size by 320 bytes increased RAM usage by ~300MB, confirming roughly one instance exists per block.
problem: Every block known to the node keeps a CBlockIndex object resident in memory. Member ordering currently places a 4-byte field between an arith_uint256 and an 8-byte uint64_t, wasting 8 bytes per object in compiler padding on 64-bit systems.

risk.why: CBlockIndex is an in-memory tracking structure not directly serialized to disk, so reordering members does not break consensus, serialization, or network protocols.

summary: Reorders member variables within CBlockIndex to group 4-byte fields together and eliminate 8 bytes of struct alignment padding on 64-bit platforms. Moving unsigned int nTx after uint64_t m_chain_tx_count aligns it next to the 4-byte nStatus field. This reduces the in-memory footprint of CBlockIndex by 8 bytes per instance across the entire block index.
